context: An interactive color palette explorer with three panels: a bar chart demoing palette colors on synthetic data, a WCAG contrast ratio matrix for all color pairs, and CVD simulation strips for protanopia/deuteranopia/tritanopia
first_impression: Structurally honest tool visualization — the bar chart has a proper zero baseline and data-driven domain, while the WCAG contrast matrix and CVD strips implement scientifically correct math.
what_works: Bar chart Y-scale uses `d3.max(data, d => d.value) * 1.1` for a data-driven domain with correct zero baseline; WCAG luminance calculation follows the sRGB standard precisely (linearization + 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722 weights) and CVD simulation applies Vienot 1999 matrices with proper gamma round-trips.
what_doesnt: Data is re-generated with an unseeded `d3.randomNormal` on every palette switch, so bar heights change between palettes making cross-palette bar comparison meaningless — a robustness failure under the permutation/subset relations; the redundant `bandW = (colors.length * 40) / colors.length` collapses to the constant 40, signaling inattention but causing no visual bug.
